title: String Formatting with the Format Operator %
code:
name = 'Arun'
age = 20
average = 82.5678

# Single and multiple value interpolation
print('Hello %s' % name)
print('Age: %d' % age)
print('Average: %.2f' % average)
print('Name: %s | Age: %d | Avg: %.2f' % (name, age, average))
explanation: Illustrates the fundamental format specifiers: %s for strings, %d for integers, and %.2f for two-decimal float rounding.

title: Creating a Formatted Tabular Report in a File
code:
students = [
    ('Arun', 85, 82.67),
    ('Priya', 92, 91.50),
    ('Rahul', 75, 74.25)
]

file = open('grades_table.txt', 'w')
file.write('%-10s %-8s %-8s\n' % ('Student', 'Mark', 'Average'))
file.write('-' * 28 + '\n')
for name, mark, avg in students:
    file.write('%-10s %-8d %-8.2f\n' % (name, mark, avg))
file.close()

# Read back and inspect
with open('grades_table.txt', 'r') as f:
    print(f.read())
explanation: Demonstrates width formatting with %-10s to align columns neatly in text file reports.

title: Command-Line Arguments with sys.argv
code:
import sys

# Simulate sys.argv invocation: python app.py report.txt 100
sys_args = ['app.py', 'records.txt', '100']

script_name = sys_args[0]
target_file = sys_args[1]
threshold = int(sys_args[2])

print('Script Name :', script_name)
print('Target File :', target_file)
print('Threshold   : %d' % threshold)
explanation: Shows how sys.argv indexes work and reminds that arguments arrive as strings requiring int() conversion.
